spec.description: Gigasim benchmark: throughput, the end-to-end latency of one block broken into the phases it blocks in, the queues that bound it, accumulated data size, and a section per store.
LittDB's write path for the block ledger. The control loop holds 64 messages and the flush loop 8; either sitting at its bound means block writes are blocking on it.
spec.title: BlockDB Queue Depth

spec.description: Blocks written to the ledger and waiting for the executor to pick them up, as the generator found the queue when it needed room. Full means execution and the state commit are the limit; empty means generation or the block ledger is. Bounded by MaxPendingExecutionQueueSize.
spec.title: Execution Queue Depth

spec.description: LittDB's write path for receipt bodies. Receipt writes block on the control loop when it fills.
spec.title: ReceiptDB Queue Depth

spec.description: The queues behind a state commit store write. The snapshot writer blocks the commit path when it fills, since a block is never dropped rather than snapshotted.
spec.title: SC Commit Queue Depth

spec.description: Blocks handed to the EVM state store and not yet applied. The commit path blocks on a full queue, which is what turns SS falling behind into slower blocks. Bounded by async-write-buffer, 100 by default.
spec.title: SS Commit Queue Depth

spec.description: How long the commit path waited for hashing to catch up. Nonzero means the benchmark is running a full MaxHashLagBlocks ahead of the hasher.
spec.title: Block Hash Wait (p99)

spec.description: Hot accounts are the fixed set most transfers draw from, cold accounts are selectable but rarely chosen, and dormant accounts exist in state but are never read.
spec.title: Account Population

spec.description: Measured by walking each store's directory, on the BackgroundMetricsScrapeInterval cadence. The state WAL lives inside the state commit store's directory, so it is counted in both.
spec.title: Database Size on Disk

spec.description: Total footprint divided by the account population, which is how the cost of state is usually quoted.
spec.title: Bytes per Account

spec.description: What the benchmark handed the ledger, against what LittDB actually wrote.
spec.title: Write Throughput

spec.description: The generator's blocking time appending a block and its QC, including the periodic flush.
spec.title: write_block Phase Latency (p99)

spec.description: The changeset offered against what Pebble wrote beneath it. The gap between them is write amplification.
spec.title: Write Throughput

spec.description: The commit path's blocking time in the state commit store, as the state DB measures it.
spec.title: commit_sc Phase Latency (p99)

spec.description: The gap between the two is what a restart replays from the WAL. A snapshot height stuck at 0 means no checkpoint has been written and a restart replays everything.
spec.title: Version & Snapshot Height

spec.description: The store's own view of its commit, one level below commit_sc.
spec.title: Internal Commit Phase Distribution

spec.description: The read path: reads served from the view cache rather than from Pebble.
spec.title: View Cache Hit Ratio

spec.description: The four Pebble databases the state commit store spreads its data across.
spec.title: Pebble Disk Usage by Sub-Store

spec.description: Bytes compaction still owes. Growing without bound means compaction cannot keep up with the write rate.
spec.title: Pebble Compaction Debt

spec.description: SS applies a block asynchronously, so what the commit path pays is the wait to hand it over. This rises only when the queue below is full.
spec.title: enqueue_ss Phase Latency (p99)

spec.description: The enqueue is what the commit path pays; the sync apply runs on the draining goroutine behind it.
spec.title: Apply Changeset Latency (p99)

spec.description: Empty until the checkpoint schedule has produced an SS snapshot.
spec.title: Snapshot Height & Duration

spec.description: Receipt bodies go to LittDB and their tag index to the log-index Pebble database.
spec.title: Write Throughput

spec.description: The commit path's blocking time writing a block's receipts. Bodies are flushed in the background, so this covers the litt handover and the synchronous log-index commit.
spec.title: write_receipts Phase Latency (p99)

spec.description: Blocks that completed every stage: generation, block write, execution, receipts and the state commit.
spec.title: Blocks / sec

spec.description: The commit path's blocking time in the state WAL. It writes without fsync, so this is normally the smallest phase of a commit.
spec.title: write_state_wal Phase Latency (p99)

spec.description: The serializer and writer queues. Either at its bound holds up the commit path.
spec.title: Queue Depth

spec.description: Bounded by the checkpoint cadence: the WAL is truncated below the newest snapshot, so a WAL that only grows means checkpoints are not being written.
spec.title: WAL Size on Disk

spec.description: How many blocks a restart would replay from the WAL right now.
spec.title: Replay Backlog

spec.description: Bytes each store was handed per second. This is the volume the benchmark asked the store to take, so it excludes whatever its engine amplifies that to; the per-store sections carry the amplified figure. state_store reads zero on a validator's stack, where SS is not opened.
spec.title: Write Throughput by Store

spec.description: The share of wall clock producers spent blocked because a queue was full, which is what back-pressure from that queue costs the stage feeding it. Depth cannot show this: it is read at whichever instant the sampler happens to run, and a queue full nearly all the time still reads empty when sampled just after a consumer drained it. A queue that never blocks reports nothing.
spec.title: Queue Blocked Time

spec.description: Every phase the goroutine that executes and commits blocks passes through, as a share of its wall clock. It is fully accounted, the wait on the block producing loop included, so these total 100%. The commit is supplied by the state DB, which is the layer that tells its three stores apart.
spec.title: Main Execution Loop — Time Spent

spec.description: What the main execution loop's execute phase is made of, sampled from a fraction of transactions set by TransactionMetricsSampleRate. Being sampled, it shows the proportions within execute rather than a share of wall clock comparable with its parent.
spec.title: └ Execute — by transaction stage

spec.description: What the main execution loop's write_receipts phase is made of: encoding the receipts, which the benchmark does itself, against handing them to the receipt store.
spec.title: └ Write Receipts — encode vs store

spec.description: What the main execution loop's commit window is made of, split across the state WAL, the state commit store and the EVM state store. These three are the second series on the top-level pie.
spec.title: └ State Commit — by store

spec.description: What the state commit store's commit_sc phase is made of. Covers the commits themselves and not the gaps between them, so it sums to its parent.
spec.title: └ SC — inside the FlatKV commit

spec.description: What the state commit's enqueue_ss phase is made of. The name is misleading: almost all of it is applying the changesets, not queueing them.
spec.title: └ SS — inside the EVM state store commit

spec.description: Every phase the goroutine that builds blocks and writes them to the block store passes through, as a share of its wall clock. Fully accounted, the blocked hand-off to the execution loop included, so these total 100%. A large wait_for_execution means execution is the limit, not block production.
spec.title: Main Block Producing Loop — Time Spent

spec.description: What the block producing loop's write_block phase is made of: the block, the QC and the AppQC covering it, and the periodic flush behind them.
spec.title: └ BlockStore Write — by record

spec.description: Every phase the goroutine that executes and commits blocks passes through, as a share of its wall clock. It is fully accounted, the wait on the block producing loop included, so these total 100%. The commit is supplied by the state DB, which is the layer that tells its three stores apart. Divided by the block rate, so each band is the time one block spends there rather than a share, which is what shows a phase getting slower while its share holds steady.

spec.description: What the execution loop's write_receipts phase is made of. The receipt bodies go to LittDB asynchronously (litt_put), but the same call also maintains the pebble index that serves eth_getLogs, and that is committed inline: stage_tag_keys builds one key per log address plus one per topic, and commit_index writes them. The index scales with logs and topics rather than with receipts, so it dominates the write.
spec.title: └ Receipt Store Write — litt vs log index

The index scales with logs and topics rather than with receipts, so it dominates the write.
